column1: # Edges of the rules OpenVerse took from Epic's verdicts on followup-book2 (#724), compile-first probes: what OpenVerse does is in each probe's header and in note (Lean and C agreeing); Epic's outcome and lines in epic_outcome and epic_lines (- where not yet compiled). Run the long-ident probes alone (single mode).

column7: note

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3509 rule (#724): F(1, 2) of F(A:[]int, ?B:int = 2), several arguments for an array parameter beside a named one. OpenVerse still makes the arguments an array, and prints result 4 If Epic refuses it (3509), an array parameter beside a named one takes no several arguments either.

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): two classes, cc and CC. The rule OpenVerse takes is the functions'; it admits two classes and prints lower 1 | upper 2 If Epic refuses it (9002, an existing type?), classes collide too.

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): a function Function() and a constant FUNCTION. OpenVerse admits them and prints lower 42 | upper 420 If Epic refuses it, a constant and a function collide too.

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): a method Function() and, in a subclass, FUNCTION(). The Book has the case commented out (FORT-793952...:346, "TODO(SOL-9082)", 9200). OpenVerse measures one class's own methods only, and prints lower 42 | upper 420 If Epic refuses it, a subclass's methods count with its parents'.

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): an interface's two methods with defaults, Function() and FUNCTION(), and a class that inherits both. OpenVerse does not measure an interface's methods, and prints lower 42 | upper 420 If Epic refuses it, an interface's methods collide as a class's do.

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): Function(X:int) beside FUNCTION(?X:int = 420), one positional, one named. OpenVerse tells them apart (a named parameter by its name) and prints lower 42 | upper 420 If Epic refuses it (9200 or 9000), a named parameter does not tell them apart.

OpenVerse: refused. Edge of the case-collision rule (#724): two functions whose names differ only in case, with one parameter type, int, under other names (A, B). Epic refuses Function(Value:int) beside FUNCTION(Value:int), 9000 (followup-book2/case-collision-same-params); does a parameter's name tell them apart? OpenVerse compares the types only, and refuses it ("have names that differ only in case and take the same parameters"). If Epic admits it, it prints lower 42 | upper 420

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the interface-implementation rule (#724): class_z := class(class_x, i_y) {}, with class_x's MethodX() = 1 and i_y's MethodX() = 3, a default this time. Epic refuses it when i_y's MethodX is abstract (3591, followup-book2/final-method-interface-nonfinal). OpenVerse admits it and, as in Java, takes the class chain's method for i_y's slot: through the interface 1 If Epic takes the interface's default: through the interface 3; it may also refuse it as ambiguous.

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the name-length rules (#724): a class of 1023 characters. Epic refuses one of 1024 (9002) and runs one of 960. OpenVerse admits names of a class up to 1023 characters and prints field 42 | method 1 If Epic refuses it, the class limit is lower (a prefix or suffix in its internal name). Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the identifier limit (#724): a field of exactly 1024 characters. Epic refuses 1025 (3655) and let a class's name of 1024 pass that check (to fail with 9002). OpenVerse admits it and prints field 42 Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the identifier limit (#724): a module function of exactly 1024 characters; the Blueprint VM's names hold 1023, as for a class (9002 at 1024). OpenVerse admits it and prints result 42 If Epic refuses it, a function's name is limited as a class's is. Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the mangled-name limit (#724): a class of 976 characters with a method Function() without parameters (the refused long-ident-mangled has Function(Param:int)). OpenVerse prints field 42 | method 1 If Epic refuses it, the parameters are not what makes the mangled name too long. Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the mangled-name limit (#724): a class of 1000 characters with a method F(). Epic refuses Function(Param:int) in a class of 976 (3655, followup-book2/long-ident-mangled) and admits F() in one of 960. OpenVerse does not check a method's mangled name, and prints field 42 | method 1 If Epic refuses it, the limit counts the class's name and the method's, whatever its parameters. Run it alone (single mode).
OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the class-name limit (#724): a struct of 1024 characters (a class of 1024 is refused, 9002). OpenVerse limits classes only, and prints field 42 Run it alone (single mode).

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3552 rule (#724): c(t) has a var field that does not mention t (var Count:int) and an immutable Data:t; F(X:t where t:type):c(t). OpenVerse admits it and prints count 2 If Epic refuses it, any var field of a parametric class counts.

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3552 rule (#724): a generic function constructs c(t) (with var Data:t) in its body, its type mentions no c. OpenVerse admits it and prints result 1 If Epic refuses it, the rule is not only about a function's type.

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the 3552 rule (#724): holder(t) has an immutable field of c(t), whose var Data:t is mutable data; F(X:t where t:type):holder(t). OpenVerse measures a class's own var fields only, and prints data 2 If Epic refuses it (3552), the rule reaches mutable data through other types' fields.

OpenVerse: refused. Edge of the spawn rule (#724): a spawn in a class's block:, which excludes no_rollback (the Book's Effects.versetest:551, 3512 for a call). OpenVerse refuses it. If Epic admits it, it prints spawned | constructed | after sleep

OpenVerse: refused. Edge of the spawn rule (#724): a spawn in an if's condition in Main. Epic refuses a spawn in a <transacts> function (3512, followup-book2); OpenVerse refuses it in a failure context too, as it refuses a call of a function without a heap specifier there ("this spawn has the 'no_rollback' effect, which a failure context does not allow"). If Epic admits it, it prints spawned | before sleep | after sleep or without spawned.

OpenVerse: ran. Edge of the spawn rule (#724): a spawn at the top of a plain <decides> function's body, which may call a function without a heap specifier (UEFN 43.12 admits followup/decides-body-default-call). OpenVerse admits it (the function is only compiled) and prints admitted

OpenVerse: refused. Edge of the 3509 rule (#724): F(1.0, 2.0, ?E := 3.0) of F(X:tuple(float, float), ?E:float = 0.1), the named argument given. OpenVerse packs nothing beside a named parameter and refuses it ("F takes 1 positional argument(s), found 2: several arguments are not packed ..."). If Epic admits it, it prints packed into the tuple
OpenVerse: ran. Control of the 3509 rule (#724): G(3, 4) of G(X:tuple(int, int)), no named parameter: the arguments pack into the tuple. OpenVerse prints packed 7
